questions.text: You unexpectedly have a completely free Saturday. How do you spend it?

answers.text: I make no plans, see what I feel like in the morning and simply go with it.
I use it for something that moves one of my own goals a real step forward.

questions.text: When do you feel most deeply at peace?

answers.text: When I am outdoors and feel part of something that has always been there.
When I have finally understood something complicated all the way through.

questions.text: Which of these bothers you more?

answers.text: When people insist on doing things by the book, even where it makes no sense.
When people do not turn up when they said they would and leave others hanging.

questions.text: You inherit an old cabin with a piece of land in the countryside. What do you do with it?

answers.text: I leave it largely as it is and look after it the way it has always been cared for.
I work out how to make the most of it, whether that means renovating, renting or selling.

questions.text: You are working on a creative project in your free time. What keeps you going?

answers.text: The satisfaction of getting it exactly right, down to the smallest detail.
The excitement itself; as long as I am burning for it, I keep at it.

questions.text: You watch a group of people working on a project together. What catches your eye first?

answers.text: Whether everyone is pulling their weight for the good of the group.
Who really holds the influence and who is just along for the ride.

questions.text: You feel stuck in a phase of life where nothing much seems to be happening. What do you do?

answers.text: I shake things up: a trip, a new hobby, anything that gets me moving again.
I let the phase run its course; things tend to shift when the time is right.

questions.text: Your club is rewriting its rules. What matters most to you about the result?

answers.text: That the rules are fair and apply to every member in exactly the same way.
That the rules are well thought through and actually work in practice.

questions.text: You walk through an old, abandoned factory site. What goes through your mind?

answers.text: I see potential: what could be made of this place and what it could be worth.
I see history, and a place that has earned the right to be left in peace.

questions.text: You receive a message from someone that really annoys you. How do you respond?

answers.text: I reply straight away and tell them honestly how it came across to me.
I wait, think through what might be behind it and only reply once I have a clear head.

questions.text: What makes a neighbourhood a really good place to live, in your eyes?

answers.text: People know each other, local traditions are kept alive and life has its rhythm.
Everyone takes responsibility for the shared spaces and keeps to what was agreed.

questions.text: You meet someone new at a friend's birthday party. What do you pick up on first?

answers.text: What they are after, and what they might bring to the table for me.
How they are feeling, and whether there is a real spark between us.

questions.text: You have to choose between two flats you both like. How do you decide?

answers.text: I compare them point by point: costs, commute, layout, and then decide.
I walk through both once more and take the one that simply feels like home.

questions.text: You do someone a big favour that costs you real effort. What makes it worthwhile for you?

answers.text: It was simply the decent thing to do; I do not need anything in return.
Favours build a network of people I can count on when I need them.

questions.text: You have just watched a film. What stays with you more?

answers.text: Whether it moved me and I felt something strong while watching it.
Whether the story held together and every detail really made sense.

questions.text: You are helping to organise a get-together for your neighbourhood. How do you go about it?

answers.text: I set up a clear plan with tasks and times, so that everything runs smoothly.
I bring people together and let the evening find its own natural shape.

questions.text: You are considering taking a course alongside your job. What draws you to it?

answers.text: Getting further: a better position, more options and more say in things.
Understanding a subject more deeply; the knowledge is a reward in itself.

questions.text: You arrive at a party where you hardly know anyone. What do you notice first?

answers.text: Whether the atmosphere is relaxed and people seem at ease with each other.
Where the energy is, and which people are clearly having the most fun.

questions.text: Your household keeps arguing about who does which chores. What do you do?

answers.text: I look at what actually takes the most time and work out a smarter way to get it all done.
I suggest a clear rota that everyone agrees to, so nobody carries more than their share.

questions.text: Imagine you were given a fully paid year off. What would make it a good year?

answers.text: Having used it to come out in a much stronger position than I went in.
Having lived it to the full, going wherever I wanted, whenever I wanted.

questions.text: Which of these bothers you more?

answers.text: People who ignore rules that exist for good reasons.
People who force changes on things that were fine as they were.

questions.text: At work, a powerful new tool is introduced that nobody really knows how to use yet. What do you do?

answers.text: I dig into how it works in detail until I properly understand what it can do.
I find the features that help my own work most and start using them right away.

questions.text: What makes a close friendship truly valuable to you?

answers.text: We can rely on each other completely, and we keep our promises.
We are free with each other: no obligations, we just want to be together.

questions.text: A friend enthusiastically tells you about a new health trend. What is your first thought?

answers.text: I am curious whether there is solid evidence behind it, and want to look into it.
I am wary; people lived simply for generations and did perfectly well.

questions.text: Your team is asked to work extra hours on a project that mostly benefits another department. What do you do?

answers.text: I only commit the extra time once I have negotiated something in return.
I pitch in. When the organisation needs it, I do my part like everyone else.

questions.text: You are choosing where to live for the next few years. What matters most to you?

answers.text: A place where I can put down roots, close to nature and to people I know.
A lively place where something new and exciting is always going on.

questions.text: Which of these bothers you more in a colleague?

answers.text: Waiting for others to hand them what they could simply go and get.
Talking confidently about things they have never properly understood.

questions.text: A group of friends wants to go on holiday together. What is your part in it?

answers.text: I push for booking the trip now and deciding everything else once we are there.
I make sure we have booked, budgeted and agreed on the plan well in advance.

questions.text: Looking back on your life one day, what would you most like to be able to say?

answers.text: That I was part of something bigger and left things in good shape.
That I went after what I wanted and did not settle for less than that.

questions.text: A meeting you attended went badly. What do you notice first when you think back?

answers.text: That the whole discussion was built on assumptions nobody had checked.
That some people simply did not stick to what we had agreed beforehand.
